name: Orange Lake and Lochloosa Lake
type: Two shallow lakes joined by Cross Creek: pads, hydrilla and floating marsh; cypress shorelines on Lochloosa
pool: Orange averages 5.5 ft;Swings about 2 ft a year; low water can close ramps
notes: Coolest water. Bass stage near the spawning flats; specks school offshore.
Spawn starts on warm spells. Big bass move shallow around the moon.
Peak spawn for bass and specks around the full moon.
Post-spawn. Shellcracker spawn on the full moon.
Shad spawn at dawn; bluegill bed on the full moon.
Summer pattern: topwater early, then mats and offshore grass.
Hottest stretch. Fish first light, last light and after storms.
Hottest water. Short bites at dawn and around storms.
Shad move shallow as the nights cool.
Fall feed. Bass school on shad in creeks and canals.
Cold fronts start the speck bite offshore.
Cold fronts. Bass on outside grass; specks school in open water.

flbass.doing: Cold fronts push bass to the outside grass lines and the deepest holes. Between fronts they slide toward the spawning flats, and the biggest fish of the year start to move.
how: Lipless crankbait or jerkbait over sparse hydrilla and eelgrass; slow it down after a front.
Punch mats with a 1 to 1.5 oz tungsten weight, or a slow Texas rig on the first hard edge.
Wild shiner under a float beside reed clumps and on outside grass: the trophy season.

specks.doing: Lochloosa is one of the best speck lakes in the state. Fish start offshore in open water and move toward the pads as spring nears.
how: Minnows, grass shrimp or jigs offshore.
Some specks carry reward tags; cut the tag off before release and report it.

bream.doing: Slow. Bluegill and shellcracker hold in deeper grass, canals and around docks; warm, sunny afternoons bring them up.
how: Grass shrimp on the bottom next to hydrilla or eelgrass.
Small jig or worm along canal edges and docks.

flbass.doing: Bass move from the outside grass toward the inside lanes and spawning flats. Warm afternoons pull them shallow; big females stage on the first hard edge.
how: Lipless or flat-sided crankbait ticking hydrilla, vibrating jig or swim jig down grass lanes.
Beaver or jig into pencil reeds and maidencane in 2 to 4 ft.
Wild shiners on the outside edge for big fish.
After a front, fish the closest deeper grass and slow down.

specks.doing: January through April is the best speck fishing on Lochloosa. Fish move from open water into the spatterdock as the water warms.
how: Grass shrimp and minnows in the spatterdock.
Drift minnows and jigs until they move in.

bream.doing: Shellcracker move onto firm sand and shell near the grass ahead of the spring full moons; bluegill feed around reeds and docks.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom with a split shot.
Crickets or grass shrimp under a small float along reeds.

flbass.doing: Spring is the best season on Orange Lake. Bass spawn around the emergent pads and the edges of the floating mats.
how: Soft plastics pitched around pads and mats.
Bag limit 5 with a 20 inch maximum; circle hooks with natural bait over 3 inches.

specks.doing: The February and March full moons often bring the best trips, with specks in the big pad fields at the north and southeast ends of Lochloosa.
how: Grass shrimp or minnows in the spatterdock.
Plan trips around the full moons.

bream.doing: Shellcracker bed on the March and April full moons on firm sand and shell near grass. Bluegill start as the water warms.
how: Red wigglers on the bottom; work the area until you find the colony.
Small beetle spin along the edge of the flat.

flbass.doing: Post-spawn bass recover on grass lines and the first drop. At dawn they hit shad spawning on reeds, riprap and hard edges, and bluegill beds pull them shallow on the full moons.
how: Buzzbait, walking bait or popping frog over pads and reeds.
Swim jig, vibrating jig or swimbait along eelgrass and hydrilla edges.
Prop bait or popper worked around the colonies.
Wacky rig or fluke around docks and cover.

specks.doing: After the spawn, specks scatter to deeper grass edges, docks, bridges and channel edges. The bite slows as the water warms.
how: Minnows at dock pilings, bridges and fish attractors.
Small jig swum along the deep edge of the vegetation.

bream.doing: April through September is bream season on both lakes, with bluegill, redear and warmouth in deep spatterdock and grass patches.
how: In deep-water spatterdock or deeper grass patches.
Grass shrimp or crickets under a cork.

flbass.doing: Bass hold in thick hydrilla, now mostly in the south half of Orange Lake, and around the pads. Spring and early summer are usually best.
how: Soft plastics, topwater and bladed jigs in the hydrilla and pads.

specks.doing: Specks scatter into open water; drift to find them.
how: Minnows and jigs across open water.

bream.doing: Good bream fishing all summer. Anchor near a thick hydrilla patch on Orange Lake, or fish the deep spatterdock on Lochloosa.
how: Grass shrimp, crickets or worms near the bottom by thick hydrilla.

flbass.doing: Shad and shiners move into creeks, canals and shoreline grass, and bass school on them. Wind-blown grass edges and points fish all day.
how: Lipless crankbait, small walking bait or swimbait at busting fish.
Vibrating jig or spinnerbait on wind-blown grass edges and reed points.
Texas rig or a weightless worm where fish are short-striking.
Shiners on outside edges as the big fish start to feed for the spawn.

specks.doing: Early in the fall, drift or troll offshore. After the first big cold front, try the pad fields.
how: Grass shrimp or minnows in the pads.

bream.doing: Bream feed hard in the grass as the water cools. Fewer beds, steady numbers.
how: Anchor near a thick hydrilla patch and fish grass shrimp or worms near the bottom.
Crickets under a cork along reed lines.
